title: Organic Chemistry I
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 200L organic chemistry curriculum, first semester: IUPAC nomenclature, structural/stereoisomerism, hybridization and bonding in organic molecules, and the chemistry of saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkanes, alkenes, alkynes), alcohols, and haloalkanes, including basic reaction mechanisms (free-radical substitution, electrophilic addition, SN1/SN2). Carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids, aromatic chemistry, and amines are reserved for CHM206.

questions.question: What is the general formula for an alkane with n carbon atoms?
questions.correct_answer: CnH(2n+2)
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons containing only single bonds, so each carbon is bonded to the maximum number of hydrogens possible, giving the general formula CnH(2n+2).

questions.question: What type of hybridization does the carbon atom in a C=C double bond of an alkene exhibit?
questions.correct_answer: sp2
questions.explanation: Each carbon in a C=C double bond is sp2 hybridized, forming three sigma bonds in a trigonal planar arrangement plus one unhybridized p orbital that forms the pi bond of the double bond.

questions.question: What type of hybridization does the carbon atom in a C=C-C triple bond (alkyne) exhibit?
questions.correct_answer: sp
questions.explanation: Carbon atoms in a triple bond are sp hybridized, forming two sigma bonds in a linear arrangement plus two unhybridized p orbitals that form the two pi bonds of the triple bond.

questions.question: What is the IUPAC name for CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3?
questions.correct_answer: Butane
questions.explanation: This is a straight-chain saturated hydrocarbon with four carbon atoms and only single bonds, named butane according to IUPAC nomenclature rules.

questions.question: In IUPAC nomenclature, how is the position of a substituent on the main carbon chain indicated?
options: By a locant number showing which carbon of the chain bears the substituent, numbered to give the lowest possible set of locants
By always numbering from the right-hand end of the molecule
By counting only hydrogen atoms present
Substituent positions are never indicated in IUPAC names
questions.correct_answer: By a locant number showing which carbon of the chain bears the substituent, numbered to give the lowest possible set of locants
questions.explanation: IUPAC rules require the main chain to be numbered so that substituents receive the lowest possible locant numbers, which are then placed before the substituent name in the compound's full name.

questions.question: What is a structural (constitutional) isomer?
options: A compound with the same molecular formula as another but a different arrangement of atoms
A compound with a different molecular formula but the same shape
Two samples of the same compound at different temperatures
A compound that differs only in isotopic composition
questions.correct_answer: A compound with the same molecular formula as another but a different arrangement of atoms
questions.explanation: Structural isomers share the same molecular formula but differ in how their atoms are connected, such as butane and 2-methylpropane, both C4H10.

questions.question: What condition is necessary for a carbon atom to be described as a chiral (stereogenic) centre?
options: It must be bonded to four different groups
It must be bonded to exactly two hydrogen atoms
It must be part of a double bond
It must be bonded to four identical groups
questions.correct_answer: It must be bonded to four different groups
questions.explanation: A chiral carbon has four different substituents attached, meaning its mirror image cannot be superimposed on itself, giving rise to two non-superimposable enantiomers.

questions.question: Cis-trans (geometric) isomerism can occur in alkenes due to restricted rotation around the C=C double bond. What is required for an alkene to show this type of isomerism?
options: Each carbon of the double bond must bear two different substituents
The molecule must contain at least three double bonds
Each carbon of the double bond must bear identical substituents
The molecule must be a straight-chain alkane
questions.correct_answer: Each carbon of the double bond must bear two different substituents
questions.explanation: Geometric isomerism arises when rotation around the C=C bond is restricted and each doubly-bonded carbon carries two different groups, allowing substituents to be arranged on the same side (cis) or opposite sides (trans).

questions.question: Which mechanism describes the reaction of methane with chlorine gas in the presence of ultraviolet light to form chloromethane?
questions.correct_answer: Free-radical substitution
questions.explanation: The reaction of alkanes with halogens under UV light proceeds via a free-radical chain mechanism involving initiation (homolytic bond cleavage), propagation, and termination steps, substituting a hydrogen atom with a halogen.

questions.question: In the free-radical chlorination of methane, what is the role of ultraviolet light in the initiation step?
options: It provides the energy needed to homolytically cleave the Cl-Cl bond, generating two chlorine radicals
It directly forms the C-Cl bond in the product
It has no chemical role and merely illuminates the reaction vessel
questions.correct_answer: It provides the energy needed to homolytically cleave the Cl-Cl bond, generating two chlorine radicals
questions.explanation: UV light supplies enough energy to homolytically break the Cl-Cl bond into two highly reactive chlorine free radicals, which then go on to abstract a hydrogen atom from methane in the propagation steps.

questions.question: Alkenes commonly undergo electrophilic addition reactions, such as the reaction with HBr. Which species initially attacks the electron-rich C=C double bond?
options: An electrophile, such as H+ (or a partially positive H in HBr)
A neutral, non-polar molecule with no partial charges
questions.correct_answer: An electrophile, such as H+ (or a partially positive H in HBr)
questions.explanation: The pi electrons of the alkene's double bond are electron-rich and attack an electrophile (electron-seeking species); in the addition of HBr, the partially positive hydrogen atom is attacked first, forming a carbocation intermediate.

questions.question: According to Markovnikov's rule, when HBr adds across an unsymmetrical alkene such as propene, where does the hydrogen atom preferentially attach?
options: To the carbon already bearing more hydrogen atoms, so the bromine attaches to the more substituted carbon
To the carbon with fewer hydrogen atoms already attached
Randomly, with no preference between the two carbons
Always to the terminal carbon of the chain regardless of substitution
questions.correct_answer: To the carbon already bearing more hydrogen atoms, so the bromine attaches to the more substituted carbon
questions.explanation: Markovnikov's rule states that in electrophilic addition to an unsymmetrical alkene, the hydrogen adds to the carbon with more hydrogens already attached, because this pathway proceeds through the more stable carbocation intermediate.

questions.question: Which simple chemical test distinguishes an alkene from an alkane by causing a colour change when the test reagent is added?
options: Bromine water turns from orange/brown to colourless in the presence of an alkene
Bromine water remains unchanged with both alkanes and alkenes
Limewater turns milky in the presence of alkenes only
Litmus paper turns blue with alkenes
questions.correct_answer: Bromine water turns from orange/brown to colourless in the presence of an alkene
questions.explanation: Alkenes rapidly decolourize bromine water via electrophilic addition across the double bond, while alkanes do not react under normal conditions, making this a standard test to distinguish saturated from unsaturated hydrocarbons.

questions.question: What distinguishes a primary alcohol from a secondary or tertiary alcohol?
options: The carbon bearing the -OH group is attached to only one other carbon atom
The carbon bearing the -OH group is attached to three other carbon atoms
It is always a gas at room temperature
questions.correct_answer: The carbon bearing the -OH group is attached to only one other carbon atom
questions.explanation: A primary alcohol has the carbinol carbon (the carbon bonded to -OH) attached to only one other carbon (or none, as in methanol); secondary alcohols have two such carbons attached, and tertiary alcohols have three.

questions.question: What is the product when a primary alcohol is oxidized by acidified potassium dichromate under mild conditions with distillation?
options: A carboxylic acid directly with no intermediate
questions.correct_answer: An aldehyde
questions.explanation: Mild oxidation of a primary alcohol (with immediate distillation to remove the product before further oxidation) produces an aldehyde; without distillation, further oxidation converts it to a carboxylic acid.

questions.question: What is the product when a secondary alcohol is oxidized by acidified potassium dichromate?
questions.correct_answer: A ketone
questions.explanation: Secondary alcohols are oxidized to ketones, which resist further oxidation under normal conditions because there is no hydrogen remaining on the carbonyl carbon to allow the reaction to proceed further.

questions.question: Why does a tertiary alcohol resist oxidation by acidified potassium dichromate under normal conditions?
options: The carbon bearing the -OH group has no hydrogen atom attached, which is required for the oxidation mechanism
Tertiary alcohols are always insoluble in the oxidizing solution
Tertiary alcohols do not contain oxygen atoms
Tertiary alcohols are less polar than primary alcohols
questions.correct_answer: The carbon bearing the -OH group has no hydrogen atom attached, which is required for the oxidation mechanism
questions.explanation: Oxidation of alcohols to carbonyl compounds requires removal of a hydrogen from the carbon bearing the hydroxyl group; since a tertiary carbinol carbon has no such hydrogen, it cannot be oxidized in the same way.

questions.question: Which mechanism, SN1 or SN2, proceeds through a planar carbocation intermediate and typically shows first-order kinetics dependent only on the substrate concentration?
questions.correct_answer: SN1
questions.explanation: The SN1 mechanism proceeds in two steps: slow ionization to form a planar carbocation intermediate, followed by rapid nucleophilic attack; the rate-determining step depends only on substrate concentration, giving first-order kinetics.

questions.question: Which mechanism, SN1 or SN2, proceeds through a single concerted step with backside attack of the nucleophile, resulting in inversion of configuration?
questions.correct_answer: SN2
questions.explanation: SN2 reactions occur in a single concerted step where the nucleophile attacks from the opposite side of the leaving group, causing inversion of stereochemistry (Walden inversion), and the rate depends on both nucleophile and substrate concentrations.

questions.question: Tertiary haloalkanes generally react via the SN1 mechanism rather than SN2. Why?
options: The bulky alkyl groups hinder backside nucleophilic attack, and the resulting tertiary carbocation is relatively stable
Tertiary haloalkanes have no leaving group at all
Tertiary haloalkanes cannot form carbocations under any circumstances
SN1 is favoured only for primary haloalkanes
questions.correct_answer: The bulky alkyl groups hinder backside nucleophilic attack, and the resulting tertiary carbocation is relatively stable
questions.explanation: Steric hindrance from three alkyl groups makes backside SN2 attack difficult, while the tertiary carbocation formed is stabilized by hyperconjugation and the inductive effect of the surrounding alkyl groups, favouring the SN1 pathway.

questions.question: What type of reaction converts a haloalkane into an alkene through loss of a hydrogen halide, typically using a strong base such as ethanolic KOH?
questions.correct_answer: Elimination reaction
questions.explanation: Elimination reactions remove a hydrogen and a halogen (as HX) from adjacent carbons of a haloalkane, forming a C=C double bond and producing an alkene; this competes with substitution reactions depending on conditions.

questions.question: Why are haloalkanes generally more reactive toward nucleophilic substitution than the corresponding alkanes?
options: The carbon-halogen bond is polarized, making the carbon electrophilic and susceptible to nucleophilic attack
Alkanes are always more polar than haloalkanes
Halogens make the molecule completely non-polar
questions.correct_answer: The carbon-halogen bond is polarized, making the carbon electrophilic and susceptible to nucleophilic attack
questions.explanation: The electronegativity difference between carbon and halogen polarizes the C-X bond, leaving the carbon with a partial positive charge that attracts nucleophiles, a reactivity absent in non-polar alkanes.

questions.question: Among the haloalkanes (C-F, C-Cl, C-Br, C-I), which carbon-halogen bond is generally the weakest and therefore reacts fastest in nucleophilic substitution?
questions.correct_answer: C-I
questions.explanation: Bond strength decreases down the halogen group (C-F is strongest, C-I is weakest) due to poorer orbital overlap with increasing atomic size, so iodoalkanes generally react fastest in nucleophilic substitution reactions.

questions.question: What is the term for compounds that have the same structural formula but differ in the spatial arrangement of atoms, such as enantiomers and diastereomers?
questions.correct_answer: Stereoisomers
questions.explanation: Stereoisomers share identical connectivity of atoms but differ in their three-dimensional spatial arrangement, a category that includes both optical isomers (enantiomers) and geometric isomers (cis-trans).

questions.question: What property do two enantiomers of a chiral molecule typically share, aside from being non-superimposable mirror images?
options: Identical physical properties such as melting point and boiling point, except for the direction they rotate plane-polarized light
Identical biological activity in all cases
questions.correct_answer: Identical physical properties such as melting point and boiling point, except for the direction they rotate plane-polarized light
questions.explanation: Enantiomers have identical physical properties in an achiral environment (melting point, boiling point, density) but rotate plane-polarized light in opposite directions and can behave very differently in chiral (e.g. biological) environments.

questions.question: What is a homologous series in organic chemistry?
options: A series of compounds with the same general formula and similar chemical properties, differing by a -CH2- unit between successive members
A group of compounds with completely unrelated structures
A series of isotopes of the same element
A group of compounds that only differ in their physical state
questions.correct_answer: A series of compounds with the same general formula and similar chemical properties, differing by a -CH2- unit between successive members
questions.explanation: A homologous series, such as the alkanes, consists of compounds following the same general formula and exhibiting a gradual, predictable change in physical properties as each successive member differs by one -CH2- unit.

questions.question: Alkynes contain a carbon-carbon triple bond. What is the general formula for a straight-chain alkyne with one triple bond and n carbon atoms?
questions.correct_answer: CnH(2n-2)
questions.explanation: A triple bond introduces two degrees of unsaturation, reducing the hydrogen count by four compared to the corresponding alkane, giving the general formula CnH(2n-2) for a single alkyne.

questions.question: Ethyne (acetylene) reacts with hydrogen in the presence of a Lindlar catalyst to stop at which stage of reduction?
options: It is only partially reduced to an alkene (ethene)
It is fully reduced to an alkane (ethane)
It is converted into an alcohol
questions.correct_answer: It is only partially reduced to an alkene (ethene)
questions.explanation: A Lindlar catalyst (palladium poisoned with lead and quinoline) selectively reduces alkynes to cis-alkenes, stopping the reaction before full reduction to the alkane occurs, unlike a standard Pd/Pt/Ni catalyst.

questions.question: What is the term for the minimum energy conformation of an alkane such as ethane, where hydrogen atoms on adjacent carbons are as far apart as possible when viewed along the C-C bond?
questions.correct_answer: Staggered conformation
questions.explanation: In the staggered conformation, hydrogen atoms on adjacent carbons are positioned as far apart as possible (60 degrees apart when viewed along the C-C bond axis), minimizing torsional strain and giving the lowest energy arrangement, as opposed to the higher-energy eclipsed conformation.

questions.question: Which reagent and conditions convert a haloalkane into an alcohol via nucleophilic substitution?
options: Aqueous sodium hydroxide (or potassium hydroxide) under reflux
Chlorine gas in the presence of UV light
questions.correct_answer: Aqueous sodium hydroxide (or potassium hydroxide) under reflux
questions.explanation: The hydroxide ion acts as a nucleophile, displacing the halide leaving group from the haloalkane to form an alcohol; aqueous conditions favour substitution, while ethanolic (alcoholic) hydroxide favours the competing elimination reaction to form an alkene.

questions.question: What does the term 'saturated' mean when describing a hydrocarbon such as an alkane?
options: The molecule contains only single carbon-carbon bonds, with the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms
The molecule is dissolved completely in water
The molecule contains at least one double or triple bond
The molecule has reached its boiling point
questions.correct_answer: The molecule contains only single carbon-carbon bonds, with the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms
questions.explanation: A saturated hydrocarbon contains only single bonds between carbon atoms, meaning each carbon is bonded to the maximum number of hydrogen atoms possible, in contrast to unsaturated hydrocarbons which contain double or triple bonds.
